blocks.text: The second enabling theme covers who decides, who measures and how the plan is run. It holds five focus areas. Three build the means of joint decision: three-tier alignment, collaboration with industry and shared policy and data (focus areas 16 to 18). Two apply them to specific gaps. Focus area 19 escalates the national deficits in infrastructure, visas and safety. Focus area 20 builds workforce skills on a labour analysis still to be commissioned.

The levers the growth case needs are spread across three tiers of government, and none of them answers to one plan. The national tier holds visa rules, air service agreements and route rights. The province holds jobs, safety programmes and infrastructure planning. Local government holds basic services and precinct management (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p58). The levers that bind growth most sit nationally (section 2.4). The province must therefore move decisions it does not make.

The bodies that should carry this work have thinned. The Department of Economic Development finds that tourism institutional capacity has eroded over a decade at provincial and municipal level (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p25). Even working partnerships lapse. FEDHASA reports that the Discover Garden Route MOU has expired, and that Knysna municipality's non-participation limited its reach (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p31). Without one provincial voice, each ask reaches the national tier from several directions or not at all.

The evidence agrees on the problem and is thin on the fix. What is needed is "a shared growth agenda with clear decision rights and joint delivery plans" (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p58). No source maps decision rights by tier beyond one summary table. The national tier is barely heard: the Department of Tourism and Stats SA spoke only to data, and SA Tourism has no recorded view (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p16, p30, p37). The first task is therefore to hear the national tier directly and write down who decides what.

Wesgro should convene the shared agenda and hold the evidence the national tier needs, rather than try to own levers it cannot. In the first quarter of 2027 the Wesgro CEO's office and DEDAT constitute a Tourism Growth Steerco (section 4.2). Wesgro's CEO and DEDAT's Head of Department co-chair it, with Cape Town Tourism as a standing member (section 4.7). Steerco agrees a decision-rights map by tier and tables the first national escalation agenda (focus area 19). It gives the province one voice and one route to national decisions.

Route work runs alongside, inside existing agreements, through standing relationships with Indian carriers and authorities and with China's state-owned carriers (MIDAS Aviation Market Assessment, Mar 2026, "The Indian Market Opportunity", "The Chinese Market Opportunity"; section 4.4).

Alignment works by settling ownership before it is contested. A decision-rights map shows each tier what it owns, so provincial and local bodies stop waiting on decisions that are theirs to make. One forum then speaks for the province, so national bodies receive one position rather than several. Where the comparators name the body that negotiates air service agreements, it is national: Chile's civil aviation board and Singapore's aviation authority (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p23, p38). The province's lever is evidence and alignment, not authority.

Coordination across tiers works where it is permanent. A public-private structure led by Visit València embeds municipal, provincial and regional authorities in one decision-making system (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p47). The change asked of the Western Cape is to embed tourism governance in permanent public-private structures (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p49). Yet coordination strains even among the leaders: in Victoria, roles and branding remain a source of tension between national and state bodies (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p16). The condition is national engagement. The plan works only if the national tier takes part in Steerco's agenda and answers its asks, which section 5.2 tracks.
